perspectives.title: Millionaire Definition
perspectives.summary: A millionaire is defined by assets or income

representative_posts.author: seanmilstead.com
representative_posts.text: I’m more of the latter definition, but with the idea that a million dollars worth of assets has to be liquid to be considered a millionaire.

representative_posts.author: vintage55.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Most people simply can't comprehend the extreme wealth, it's an abstract. Hell, I was in my 40's making somewhere around $15K/year and raising a family, when I actually put $1,000,000 into context and realized a million a year was more per week than I was making in a year.

representative_posts.author: andrewswrightmd.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I would say millionaire has a million in capital (not necessarily all liquid assets, but accessible), so not including home or retirement accounts.

representative_posts.author: yalestewart.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I do NOT believe that we would ever call someone who simply came into possession of something worth one million or more dollars to also be a millionaire, unless speaking of them under the assumption that they would immediately cash in said asset for one million dollars.

representative_posts.author: gwillow.me
representative_posts.text: I guess since billionaire is obviously total assets, not income, the second makes more sense. But that means a lot of people in high-COL areas are millionaires on paper by dint of the value of their house, but their real-life spending power hardly reflects that...

representative_posts.author: djangowexler.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think you're correct here, but also it's true that the value of "millionaire" has eroded a lot with inflation! It's now less "independently wealthy" and more "mid-career tech worker or moderately prosperous dentist".

representative_posts.author: mlhumphrey.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think of it as net worth. So if you have a $1 million house but owe $950K on it, not a millionaire. But $1.5 million house and owe $500K, then a millionaire.

representative_posts.author: mikeyalexander.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I’ve never considered this at that level before, but I think I would classify both as millionaires. A finer point would be anyone with an annual income of $1M, or total assets exceeding $1M, would be a multi-millionaire. But I’m not going to hate on them until they’re pushing past $50M in assets.

representative_posts.author: phrly.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think the definition in popular parlance has moved from $1 million of assets to $1 million income. Mostly because $1 million of assets used to be enough to be rich without needing to work more, and now it's decidedly not.

representative_posts.author: garjones.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I agree, it was assets (and is used that way for billionaires now, nobody has that as a salary) but in 1969 my patents' house cost 3k. So many with property assets now can be a millionaire it doesn't stand up as an indicator of being really rich.

representative_posts.author: spicycurry.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Traditionally, assets, today I think colloquial usage means more “income” because most people wouldn’t describe the average Seattle homeowner as a millionaire.

representative_posts.author: smpa.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Also a lot of the people I would call millionaires don't have any non-investment/retirement income, or it varies *dramatically*. Major performer incomes are completely insane; they have years where it's basically zero. The unpredictability is part of why so many popular performers end up bankrupt.

representative_posts.author: gwillow.me
representative_posts.text: Speaking of money, help settle something: I always thought a millionaire was somebody who earned a million dollars a year. But apparently there is another camp that thinks a millionaire is someone whose *total assets* are a million dollars or more. Which is correct?

representative_posts.author: zackdavisson.com
representative_posts.text: Definitely assets. Technically I am a millionaire due to my house. Shockingly, that does not transfer to income.

representative_posts.author: okazu.yuricon.com
representative_posts.text: I agree, but kind of hate that, as that makes my wife and I millionaires because we own a home (paid off after 25 years last year) in an absurdly expensive area. I assure you we are not millionaires. That price could crash any day

representative_posts.author: cass-izzy.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The latter - being a millionaire isn't nearly as impressive as it was when I was a child.

representative_posts.author: seeyouinnj.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think colloquially most people use it to mean “has more than a million dollars in assets” with some flexibility over whether you count just liquid capital or include their house or business.

representative_posts.author: yalestewart.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I can't speak for the ENTIRE Midwest, but I feel pretty strongly that at least regionally, we consider anyone who is currently in possession of one million or more dollars to be a millionaire.

representative_posts.author: gplowe92.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Related question how does it work for couples, like are Paige and I both millionaires if we have a million in assets or does it need to be 2 mil since there are two of us?

representative_posts.author: patstuffns.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: If you're assets less your liabilities is $1MM, then you're a millionaire. If you sell your house for a mil and use it to pay off the 975K you owe on your mortgage.....sorry.

representative_posts.author: andykhouri.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Bravo’s MILLIONAIRE MATCHMAKER calculated it by net worth, and I can’t imagine a better standard for it than gold diggers.

representative_posts.author: jaqrabbit.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It's an inflation problem. It used to refer to assets (in the Bruce Wayne era), but inflation made that irrelevant: a middle-class boomer with a house in the right location has a million-dollar estate.

representative_posts.author: braak.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Yeah especially in the US, statistics like "80% of millionaires are self-made" is really just a way of saying a lot of people bought houses cheap in the 80s that are worth a lot more now.

representative_posts.author: ulisesr.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: awww mark wants the extra couple million $$$ to add to his 200+ BILLION collection which of course is less than 0.1% of his wealth :)

representative_posts.text: Nooooo fuck no its not about what I count as wealth. Because I think people are all fucking insane. There is no way in hell my property is worth $2.2 million its a bullshit inflated valuation ALL property in the US is bullshit inflated valuation. Does not change the DATA

representative_posts.author: airshipchronos.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: But also the 2nd definition is obviously correct. The 1st also correct. A millionaire can be either or or both. if you own your house, yes that is wealth that you have.

representative_posts.author: eugenehetzel.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: 2 mil today would have been 375000 when I was born. Following monetary inflation alone, not cost inflation, 2 million will likely be worth half that (at least) in 2056. I do not assume earnings increases that would be commiserate. So your math is simply off for a person born in 1976 as I was.

representative_posts.author: coffeeindiana.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I don't think you know what being poor is like and how little money it takes where small improvements are life changing. 190 million people live with a net worth of $60k or less. Giving them a net worth increase of 50%+ would absolutely change their lives.

perspectives.title: Belmont's Curse
perspectives.summary: Belmont's Curse is a good game

representative_posts.author: phantomstormsilver.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I'm close to five hours in the new Castlevania, and I've been playing these games for a good long while by now. Internet's clearly on something, trying to say it's bad or "not Castlevania". Belmont's Curse is a blast. Yeah, it's different and probably not in my top 10 but what's the problem?

representative_posts.author: thenesta.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I played some Castlevania Belmont's Curse and I don't think I actually like it? I don't think it's a terrible game or anything, but it doesn't feel like Castlevania to me. I know there are accessibility settings, but the game feels a little too difficult for my taste for this kind of game by default

representative_posts.author: loksr.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse is pretty great so far, and I’m super grateful for the difficulty adjust options as I’m just not that good at this sort of game anymore!

representative_posts.author: ikaricat.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Another day, another stream full of awesome games and great company! We're back with MORE Castlevania: Belmont's Curse as I attempt to full clear 100% the game on my first try! Let's see how well I do.

representative_posts.author: werewolf-witch.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: My feelings for Belmont's Curse are entirely biased but it feels so refreshing to have a Good Castlevania again. Like, it's been so long and so many years of Konami trying to feed us slop, and then Belmont's was made with religious love and devotion to the entire series.

representative_posts.author: metataros.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The one-two punch of Belmont's Curse and the VS DLC of Ode to Castlevania could make a man cry seeing the absolute pillar of one of, if not his favorite game series, back from the dead after 18 years

perspectives.title: Universal Healthcare

representative_posts.author: 1voter.org
representative_posts.text: Healthcare in the US is stupid. 1. It's tied to employment. Think about that. 2. The entire system is FOR PROFIT. In other words, for every time your insurance company denies a claim, they MAKE money. Think about that. 3. There are so many "middlemen" all FOR PROFIT in between you and your doctor.

representative_posts.author: raging-dee.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: We need universal healthcare. Dems should be running on this. We are all sick of our expensive, piecemeal healthcare system, with Wall Street and greed making decisions on our care instead of our doctors.

representative_posts.author: hazelazureus.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: the insurance companies are the only ones with any power to approve or deny healthcare anymore in this country; doctors themselves are as much trapped under the bullshit as patients.

representative_posts.author: sturdycat.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: We have more people working in health INSURANCE than healthcare. WTAF

representative_posts.author: economymedicine.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: My point is that frequently in these debates single payer or nationalized health services are treated as if nobody will ever have disputes over coverage, wait times or prices. They are not magical systems they involve choices and tradeoffs like everything else even I believe they are better.

representative_posts.author: rogerdoggie.bsky.social

Other.name: Bad Parents

perspectives.title: Toxic Parents

representative_posts.author: docmcohen.medsky.social
representative_posts.text: Exactly. And the only thing that this reveals is just how thoroughly these parents ignored the countless attempts made by their kids to preserve the relationship by establishing boundaries and/or asking for basic human consideration and kindness.

representative_posts.author: smalladventures.net
representative_posts.text: Aren't... parents definitionally the people who had kids anyway? The ones who knew aren't parents. I guess maybe they know *now*.

representative_posts.author: kiddocut.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This was inevitable in modern America, these “parents” are seeing the consequences of their neglect in complete no contact and now are panicking enough to vote in the worst possible people in office to make sure their kids *know* they still have some level of control. It’s fucking evil.

representative_posts.author: iezeradd.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I hate how it's being treated like a new phenomenon to blame on millennials when people have been cutting ties with shitty abusive parents since the dawn of time

representative_posts.author: domoffinland.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: parents sort your shit out and stop using your kids as a substitute for a sense of self

representative_posts.author: amandafarough.ca
representative_posts.text: Anyway, being a parent can be really hard sometimes (especially in the early years), but holy shit does it pay off when they get older and they turn out to be THIS AWESOME.

representative_posts.author: lhertzel.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Sometimes it’s the parent cutting off the kid.

representative_posts.author: missivonne.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Donald Trump thinks everyone's as bad a parent as he is. Like he'd notice his children were gone for 3 or 4 days.

representative_posts.author: sjgochenour.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: (and I don't think it is a widespread problem by any means, given the number of people I know who are still fighting to maintain some semblance of a relationship with a wretched parent.)

representative_posts.author: kat-otis.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I love seeing good parents. They can be hard to find, these days.

representative_posts.author: rebelliousnature.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Sometimes I think of all the missteps I've had as a parent and I get down on myself, and then I read about shit like Kate Gosselin and I'm like 'ok, I'm not THAT bad..." Seriously, how hard is it to not be a piece of shit, tell your kid you love them, maybe not lock them in a fucking closet?

representative_posts.author: moonlitwomyn.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Reality hits hard on the disillusionment of our parents...🤔😉

representative_posts.author: fangofthesun.bsky.social

They eventually told me "yeah you should have been swallowed, it was a bad choice to have you" and now that I'm gone they're sad and resentful that I'm not in their life Make up your fucking mind

representative_posts.author: thepaulruby.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: spiderchomper.com

representative_posts.author: carogonza.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: You know it's the parents.

representative_posts.author: ceruleanbutterfly.bsky.social

representative_posts.author: realcinematik.bsky.social

My mom had no idea from age 6-16 as to whether her dad was even still alive: he divorced her mom & disappeared.

representative_posts.author: pileque.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The parents didn't notice that their kids disappeared for "3 or 4 days"??

representative_posts.author: gabyhinsliff.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: i wrote one of the pieces linked here, and uh, that's exactly what it did question. Family breakdown is unbelievably complicated, different in every case, not for outsiders to second-guess. It's not served by people leaping to glib universal conclusions - either about the kids or the parents.

representative_posts.author: g--0.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: part of the reason it works like this is because boomer parents have been given permission to just dump any objections to their parenting style into the pathology bucket "oh you think I made mistakes? Well that's just the crazy talking" then they don't get why people pick estrangement

representative_posts.author: almarosar572.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: What a person themselves do ..speak ..act on or not act on PROVES who THEY ARE ..mommy or daddy dearest actions DOES NOT make them the same type of person that their parent(s) were / are

representative_posts.author: gordonhodsonphd.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: In the past, for instance, homophobic father could be a bigot to their LGBT adult child. Society supported him in this bigotry, & the child "put up with it". Now parents have to WORK at maintaining relations with their children, and many don't have the will, motivation, or the right priorities.

representative_posts.author: ohcarolinian.bsky.social
